match.reason: The closest bank point, Context and values in paired texts, teaches comparing two texts that share a story, while this point asks how one text's context, values and the writer's choices reveal what the author supports or criticises, so it is a related but narrower idea.

draft.title: Views and values of the author
card: A text is written at a certain time and in a certain place. Its historical context is that setting, including the events, laws and attitudes of the period.
Values are beliefs about what matters, such as fairness, loyalty or tradition. A text can reflect the values of its society, or it can question them.
A writer makes choices: which characters to admire, who gets punished, and what tone to use. These choices hint at what the writer supports or criticises.
Write about the writer's views as what the text suggests, using evidence. Avoid claiming to know what the writer really thought or intended.
draft.remember: Context and the writer's choices point to the values a text supports or criticises.

a.q: In a novel, a cruel landowner is mocked and ends up ruined. What do the writer's choices most likely suggest?
opts: The text criticises the landowner's behaviour
The text admires the landowner's power
The text has no view about the landowner
The text only describes the period's history
a.why: Mockery and a ruinous ending are choices that invite the reader to judge the landowner harshly. The text is not neutral, because the writer has shaped how the reader responds.
a.clue: Think about how the writer treats the landowner.

b.q: A student writes: 'The author hated the class system and wanted to end it.' Why is this a weak way to discuss the author's views?
opts: It states the author's private feelings as proven fact
It names the class system, which is not a value
It links the text to its historical context
It uses the writer's choices as evidence
b.why: The sentence states the author's private feelings and aims as fact, and gives no evidence from the text. A stronger sentence would say what the text suggests about the class system through its characters and events. Mentioning context is not the problem.
b.clue: Can a reader know what the author felt inside?

a.best: The text criticises the landowner's behaviour

b.best: It states the author's private feelings as proven fact
